name: brand-film
title: Brand film
summary: A two-to-six-minute 16:9 film that tells a brand's whole story: what it is, why it matters, how it works and what it unlocks. The shape of the films Slate was built from.
use_when: The brand needs its flagship: the film for the website and YouTube that every shorter cut comes from.

pace.note: The films' own placement: a line starts 0.3 s into its shot, the next shot starts 0.3 s after it ends, and an act break breathes for 0.9 s.

beats.name: hook
beats.job: One idea or question the viewer can't ignore, inside the first five seconds.

beats.name: tension
beats.job: The problem, or the world before: why this matters now.

beats.name: reveal
beats.job: What the brand is, named plainly.

beats.name: how it works
beats.job: The product or idea in three steps or fewer, shown working rather than listed.

beats.name: proof
beats.job: Sourced numbers, the real product and approved claims only.

beats.name: what it unlocks
beats.job: The viewer's life after: outcomes, not features.

beats.name: close
beats.job: The lockup and one call to action that says where to go.

rules: One signature moment per act: the beat people remember and retell.
On-screen words support the voice instead of repeating it; when the text repeats the voice, people read instead of listening.
Carry objects across cuts instead of hard-cutting in and out of section cards.
No long static holds: give every contrast in the voice something to look at.
Body copy big enough to read at video size; the read-time gate checks every hold.
End on a call to action with somewhere to go. For YouTube, keep the last 5 to 20 seconds calm enough for end screens.

captions.position: drawn by the player from the sidecar files

budget.note: What the first brand films spent; the voice-over range includes tag A/B takes.

notes: The hero film. Every social cut-down, aspect or language version is a derived film of this one (slate variant), reusing its approved takes and timings by reference.
A supervised brand film is finished in After Effects, started by the person who supervises it.
Set broadcast: true in film.json before it airs on TV or in a cinema: broadcast loudness and an Eleven Music Enterprise licence.
